_comment: The public-domain slice of the OMR benchmark (eerovil/musescore-choir-plugins#83).
Paths are relative to the repository root. Bounds are fractions of page height,
the same units .systems.json uses, so they crop correctly at any resolution.
See README.md for what travelled and what stayed on the host.

pages.title: Herää Suomi! printed p.420, bars 11-17 — good scan
pages.parts: TTBB (T.I/T.II on a treble staff sounding an octave down, B.I/B.II on a bass staff)
pages.notes: The only page with note-level ground truth. 120 note events. Bar 15 in the bass is the exception: the two basses are in unison and the print has a single line, so the truth is one voice there.

pages.title: Herää Suomi! printed p.420, bars 11-17 — poor scan
pages.parts: TTBB (T.I/T.II on a treble staff sounding an octave down, B.I/B.II on a bass staff)
pages.notes: The same music and the same truth as B1a at a worse scan, so scan quality is isolated from everything else. Its own bounds: this copy sits about a tenth of a page lower than B1a's.

pages.title: Virta venhettä vie printed p.119, bars 15-30
pages.notes: No copy of its own: page 2 of the song fixture's source PDF is this page, rasterising pixel for pixel identically to the host benchmark's extract. 19th-c engraving, divisi written as stacked noteheads in most bars, and the meter moves 4/4 -> 3/4 at the end of system 3 and 3/4 -> 2/4 -> 4/4 inside system 4. Structural reference only — nobody has compared the fixture's cleaned score against the print end to end.
